scope: Two Motion subtopics, original-question layout demonstration, not a real ExamSIDE corpus

records.raw_stem: Start at +1 m. Walk 5 m left, then 3 m right. Find the final position, distance and displacement.
records.raw_answer: Final position −1 m; distance 8 m; displacement −2 m (left).

hints.h1: Keep the starting coordinate separate from the lengths walked.
hints.h2: Mark the start, the turning point and the finish on a number line.
hints.h3: The turning point is at +1 − 5 m. Find the finish next.

solution.why: Position changes carry direction; path lengths do not.
solution.method: Track the walk step by step: start at +1 m, walk 5 m left to reach 1 − 5, then walk 3 m right to reach the final position, 1 − 5 + 3. Distance simply adds both leg lengths, 5 + 3, while displacement compares only the final position to the start, −1 − (+1).
solution.answer: Final position −1 m; distance 8 m; displacement −2 m (left).
solution.keep: The final coordinate is not automatically the displacement.

records.raw_stem: An object moves from −2 m to +5 m without reversing. Find its distance and displacement. Explain the signs.

hints.h1: Crossing the origin does not mean reversing direction.
hints.h2: Draw −2, 0 and +5 in order along the line.
hints.h3: The first part of the path, from −2 m to 0 m, is 2 m.

solution.why: The route goes 2 m to zero and another 5 m right.
solution.method: Distance adds the two legs of the actual path travelled: 2 m to reach zero, then 5 m more to +5 m, giving 2 + 5. Displacement instead compares only the two endpoints, final position minus initial position: +5 − (−2).
solution.keep: Equal distance and displacement size require no reversal in this straight-line journey.

records.raw_stem: Two students start at 0 m and finish at +4 m. Must they have travelled the same distance? Draw two journeys to support your answer.
records.raw_answer: No. These distances are 4 m and 10 m; both displacements are +4 m.

hints.h1: The question fixes the endpoints, not the route.
hints.h2: Draw one direct route and one route with a turn.
hints.h3: For the turning route, choose a turning point beyond +4 m.

solution.why: Endpoints fix displacement but leave the path undecided.
solution.method: One can go directly 0 → +4. Another can go 0 → +7 → +4. Their paths are 4 m and 7 + 3 m.
solution.answer: No. These distances are 4 m and 10 m; both displacements are +4 m.
solution.keep: A drawing can disprove an “always” claim.

records.raw_stem: A particle goes from −3 m to +5 m, then returns to +1 m. Find distance and displacement. A second observer adds 10 m to every coordinate. What changes?
records.raw_answer: Distance 12 m and displacement +4 m for both origins. Positions change.

hints.h1: The second observer changes the labels, not the physical journey.
hints.h2: Draw the three positions, then label each with 10 m added.

solution.why: Displacement is a coordinate difference, so a common shift cancels.
solution.method: Path lengths: 5 − (−3) = 8 m and 5 − 1 = 4 m. Δx = 1 − (−3) = +4 m. Shifted endpoints are +7 m and +11 m.
solution.answer: Distance 12 m and displacement +4 m for both origins. Positions change.
solution.keep: A reference origin changes position values, not a fixed journey.

records.raw_stem: Journey A: +3 m/s for 4 s, then +2 m/s for 2 s. Journey B changes only the last velocity to −2 m/s. Find both distances and displacements. Explain what stays the same.
records.raw_answer: A: Δx = +16 m, distance 16 m. B: Δx = +8 m, distance 16 m.

hints.h1: Only the direction of the last interval changes.
hints.h2: Sketch the two graphs with the same scales.
hints.h3: Calculate the common first area: (+3 m/s) × (4 s).

solution.why: Reversing the second velocity changes the area sign, not its size.
solution.method: First area is +12 m in both. The last area is +4 m in A and −4 m in B. Add signs for displacement and sizes for distance.
solution.answer: A: Δx = +16 m, distance 16 m. B: Δx = +8 m, distance 16 m.
solution.keep: A sign change can alter the endpoint without altering total path.

records.raw_stem: Use the graph to find displacement and distance from 0 s to 5 s. Give a physical meaning for each area.
records.raw_answer: Displacement +2 m; distance 14 m. The parts mean 8 m right and 6 m left.

hints.h1: Read the duration of each horizontal segment.
hints.h2: Separate the two rectangular regions at t = 2 s.

solution.why: Graph widths are durations. The second width is 5 − 2 = 3 s.
solution.method: Signed areas are +4 × 2 = +8 m and −2 × 3 = −6 m. For distance count both path lengths.
solution.answer: Displacement +2 m; distance 14 m. The parts mean 8 m right and 6 m left.
solution.keep: Read each width from its endpoints before multiplying.

records.raw_stem: A robot has the graph shown and starts at x = −5 m. Find its distance, displacement and final position after 7 s.
records.raw_answer: Distance 12 m; displacement +4 m; final position −1 m.

hints.h1: The starting coordinate is separate from the displacement.
hints.h2: Pair the graph regions with right, stopped and left motion arrows.
hints.h3: The final region has duration 7 − 3 s.

solution.why: Rest adds no displacement. Final position is start plus signed change.
solution.method: Areas are +8 m, 0 m and −4 m. Add their sizes for distance and their signed values for displacement. Then add the change to −5 m.
solution.answer: Distance 12 m; displacement +4 m; final position −1 m.
solution.keep: A positive displacement can finish at a negative coordinate.

records.raw_stem: The velocity follows the straight graph shown. Find distance and displacement over 4 s. At what time does the particle reverse direction? Justify this from the graph.
records.raw_answer: Displacement +8 m; distance 10 m; reversal at 3 s.

hints.h1: Locate the zero crossing before calculating areas.
hints.h2: Use the straight-line change to split the graph into two triangles.
hints.h3: The velocity decreases by 8 ÷ 4 m/s each second.

solution.why: Reversal occurs where velocity changes sign; split the signed area there.
solution.method: Velocity falls 8 m/s in 4 s. It reaches zero after 6 ÷ 2 = 3 s. Areas: +½ × 3 × 6 = +9 m; −½ × 1 × 2 = −1 m.
solution.answer: Displacement +8 m; distance 10 m; reversal at 3 s.
solution.keep: Equal endpoint signs are not the test; inspect the sign throughout the interval.
